title: cross-domain-stability-bootcamp-sprint-plan-2027
content:
Purpose and high-level goal:
This doc defines a 6-week, cross-domain "stability bootcamp" to accelerate SLO adoption, operational handoffs, and triage readiness across product feature teams, platform, serving runtime, and SRE. The bootcamp is a focused, hands-on program to reduce time-to-resolve, improve SLO signal quality, and create a standing cohort of "stability liaisons" embedded in feature teams.

Why this approach (context):
- We have strong SLO theory and many one-off playbooks, but adoption is uneven across feature teams.
- Observability gaps (missing cardinality, flaky tracing, weak error annotations) slow diagnosis and increase toil.
- A short, intensive program that pairs platform/SRE with feature teams will create repeatable onboarding artifacts and measurable impact on latency/availability KPIs.

Audience:
- Primary: feature-team leads (backend/product), platform-engineering, serving-runtime engineers, SREs.
- Secondary: product managers, solutions engineering, support oncall coordinators.

Outcomes (what success looks like at end of 6 weeks):
- 6 feature teams with embedded stability liaisons trained and run a minimum of 3 SLO experiments each.
- Runbooks updated for common failure modes with triage steps and instrumentation checks.
- Mean time to detection (MTTD) reduced by 30% for covered services; mean time to mitigate (MTTM) reduced by 25%.
- One shared "decision ledger" for SLO changes + canary/rollback decisions.

Scope (what's in/out):
In scope:
- SLO definition alignment and error budget experiments for selected services (list to be finalized).
- Observability audits (logs, traces, metrics cardinality) and instrumentation fixes.
- Oncall triage playbook pairing and simulation drills.

Out of scope (for this run):
- Full infra-only migrations (e.g., wholesale telemetry stack changes). Those are tracked as follow-ups.

Program structure (6-week cadence):
Week 0 (prep, onboarding):
- Kickoff + intake forms (feature teams submit current SLOs, oncall rotation, known pain points).
- Baseline metrics snapshot (latency p50/p95, error rate, MTTD/MTTM).
- Assign "stability liaison" (1 platform/SRE + 1 serving-runtime SME paired with each feature team).

Weeks 1-2 (audit + quick wins):
- Observability audit checklist run (missing tags, trace sampling issues, slow queries) by liaison pair.
- Deploy 1-2 low-risk instrumentation fixes (log context, error codes, alert dedup).
- Weekly show-and-tell: 30-minute demo of findings and immediate mitigations.

Weeks 3-4 (SLO experiments & runbook drafting):
- Define experiment: hypothesis, success criteria, guardrails (error budget, customer impact). Use templated experiment sheet.
- Canary plan & rollback criteria drafted and validated with platform oncall.
- Draft runbook for top 3 failure modes discovered during audit.

Week 5 (simulation & launch):
- Tabletop simulation: inject realistic failure scenarios (time-limited load spike, auth downstream outage). Run triage with liaison, feature team, and backup oncall.
- Launch SLO experiment (canary or trial threshold adjustment). Monitor signals and collect decision data.

Week 6 (retro + handoff):
- Retro with all cohorts. Capture decisions in decision ledger.
- Finalize runbooks, tag PRs for instrumentation changes, and record follow-up backlog.
- Handoff: stability liaison reduces active pairing and hands ownership to feature team oncall.

Roles and responsibilities (brief):
- Program lead: Asha Ramirez (platform-engineering) — overall schedule, intake, decisions.
- Stability liaison (per feature team): 1x SRE/platform + 1x serving-runtime engineer (embedded during weeks 1-5).
- Feature team lead: provide context, prioritize fixes, own PRs.
- Observability SME: run audit template and implement quick fixes.
- SRE oncall: validate canary/rollback plan and be triage backup during simulations.

Key artifacts (deliverables):
- Team intake sheet (spreadsheet) — baseline metrics + SLOs (owner: Asha).
- Observability audit report (template) — checklist + remediation PR links.
- SLO experiment sheet (template) — hypothesis, metrics, rollbacks, timeframe.
- Runbook PRs merged to internal runbook repo.
- Decision ledger entry per team (confluence page or single journal).

Acceptance criteria for completed team workstream:
- Audit items: at least 70% of high-severity observability gaps remediated or triaged to backlog with owners.
- SLO experiment: hypothesis and monitoring dashboards live; experiment runs for minimum 7 days with decision recorded.
- Runbooks: at least one runbook merged and referenced from the service README.

Metrics and how we'll measure impact (data sources):
- Baseline + weekly snapshots of error-rate, p95 latency, MTTD, MTTM (source: observability dashboards).
- Alert noise reduction (count of alerts per week pre/post).
- Experiment success: maintained error budget / reduced noisy alerts.

Risk register (top items) and mitigations:
- Risk: Feature teams deprioritize bootcamp work because of feature ship deadlines. Mitigation: executive sponsor (product lead) required on kickoff; limit pair time to 20% of liaison's sprint allocation.
- Risk: Instrumentation PRs introduce regressions. Mitigation: require canary + test harness for all changes; small, incremental PRs.
- Risk: Observability quota or cost spike. Mitigation: use sampling and focused dashboards for experiments; revert to previous sampling after test window.

Communications plan:
- Weekly digest to reliability-all with highlights and links.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder review (30 minutes) with product and platform leadership.
- Decision ledger public to participating teams and SREs.

Training & knowledge transfer:
- Two live workshops (recorded): "SLO experiment design" and "Fast triage for model-serving incidents".
- Quick reference cheat-sheet for triage (1-page).

Operational templates (links below) — to be finalized in Confluence:
- Experiment template (fields: hypothesis, target metric, guardrails, measurement windows).
- Observability audit checklist (fields: metrics, traces, logs, sampling, tags).
- Runbook template (fields: detection, mitigation steps, verification, escalation).

Follow-up backlog (expected outcomes post-bootcamp):
- Platform: prioritized telemetry investments (instrumentation libs, improved span naming).
- Product/feature teams: absorb liaison learnings and own runbook maintenance.
- SRE: incorporate successful experiment policies into SLO governance.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Final list of participating teams by 2026-12-22 (ask PM org).
- Confirm executive sponsor from Growth/Prod.
- Need budget headcount for liaison time (approx 0.2 FTE per liaison over 6 weeks).
- Decide persistent location for decision ledger: Confluence page or central Git-backed journal?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Send intake form to nominated teams and request metric snapshots (owner: Asha).
- Book kickoff (30–45 mins) and workshop slots (owners: Asha + Marco).
- Pre-populate audit checklist for first two pilot teams (owners: Sofia + Drew).

Appendix (links and quick refs):
- Suggested pilot teams: Payments API, Chat Routing, Embeddings Service (proposed).
- Quick JIRA templates to use: REL-EXPT- template (create per-team experiment ticket).
- Contact list: Program lead (Asha Ramirez), Observability SME (Marco Chen), SRE oncall coordinator (Tara Nguyen).

Notes on tone and doc status: this is a working doc; expect changes after kickoff. Action items are intentionally low-friction: small PRs, focused experiments, pair-first approach.

---
Decision history (bootstrap):
- 2026-12-01: Program concept approved by platform director (informal).
- 2026-12-10: Pilot teams proposed by product managers.

(End of doc)
